title: SDK Quickstart capture board — Apr 22 2026
content:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 10:30-11:00 PT (standup/captureboard)
Location: Zoom + ephemeral whiteboard
Facilitator: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya, Luis, Priya, Zoe, Tom, Kelsey

Purpose: quick sync to unstick blocked quickstart items for the public SDK + short checklist to get the new JS/Go quickstarts stable for the next docs deploy. Keep this lightweight, capture action owners + due dates.

Top of mind (1 sentence each)
- Maya: finalizing QA checklist for JS quickstart, need a smoke-test harness for CI.
- Luis: sample app network flakiness with Dedicated auth flow — reproduced on staging.
- Priya: docs PR for token best practices in progress, waiting on SDK API final names.
- Zoe: pod for release notes + changelog automation; small YAML fix needed.
- Tom: E2E runner failing intermittently on long sequences (>2k tokens) in node client.
- Kelsey: quickstart narrative (onboarding copy) draft is 80% — needs screenshots.

Progress updates (short bullets)
- JS quickstart: local dev flow validated on mac (Node14/18), added explicit install of optional native bindings. PR #1423 opened for sample app and README updates (linked). TODO: add CI smoke test that runs the example for 30s. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-04-27.
- Go quickstart: minimal example done, module path changed to github.com/redwood-inference/examples/go-quickstart; needs vetting for dep pinning and cross-compile in CI. Owner: Luis. ETA: 2026-04-29.
- Docs: token-management section draft (docs repo PR #89) includes KMS example but missing SDK call examples — blocked on API name stability. Owner: Priya. Blocker: SDK rename proposal.
- Samples repo: added a conversational sample that demonstrates streaming + function calling; tests failing when run behind corporate proxy. Owner: Tom. Next step: add proxy env test matrix.

Blockers & troubleshooting notes
- Dedicated auth (Luis): staging returns 401 for a subset of refresh flows. Repro steps attached in GH issue; likely a race when token cache is cleared. Workaround: restart service; need deeper investigation. Suggested pairing with infra team this week. Condition: blocking release of Dedicated quickstart.
- E2E flake (Tom): node runner hits memory leak when generating long completions; suspect KV cache not freed in the node native binding. Repro: run long-seq test with --record-trace; heap grows. Action: create minimal repro and open issue against native-binding.
- Screenshots for Kelsey: CI image runner doesn't have the browser toolchain; using pre-captured screenshots is OK for now, but long-term we should have a headless capture job in CI.

Decisions from this session
- Ship JS quickstart without native bindings auto-install (explicit opt-in) to reduce install surface for first-time users. Follow-up: add opt-in section in README and mention performance caveat. Owner: Maya.
- Delay Go quickstart cross-compile automation to next sprint; prioritize stability first. Owner: Luis.

Action items (owner / due)
- Maya: Add CI smoke test that spins up the JS example and hits a short generation endpoint (30s). Due 2026-04-27.
- Tom: Create minimal repro for node native-binding leak and open GH issue with heap profile + trace. Due 2026-04-24.
- Priya: Update docs PR to include provisional SDK call samples (use current API names) with a note about upcoming rename. Due 2026-04-25.
- Luis: Pair with infra on Dedicated auth race; schedule 60m debug session. Due 2026-04-23.
- Kelsey: Produce 6 screenshots (onboarding, quickstart run, error handling) and drop into samples/assets. Due 2026-04-26.
- Zoe: Fix YAML for changelog pipeline and add a lightweight release-note generator script. Due 2026-04-28.

Notes to self / loose ideas (informal)
- Consider adding a "quickstart smoke badge" that runs a daily cron on a small instance and reports status in the README. Low overhead, high signals.
- We should include a small table in each quickstart that explains tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs private (one-liner each) — helps PMs and enterprise readers.
- Idea: interactive playground embedded in docs (sandbox) that uses ephemeral API keys and rate-limits; might need product sign-off for billing model.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: shipping quickstarts that encourage users to enable native bindings by default may cause crash reports and higher support load. Mitigation: opt-in messaging + clear troubleshooting doc.
- Risk: Dedicated auth instability blocks enterprise onboarding. Mitigation: pair with infra + escalate if no progress within 48h.

Follow-ups / meeting cadence
- Quick sync (15m) Mon/Wed this week at 10:30 PT to move items fast (attendance optional except owners).
- Deep debugging session (60m) for Dedicated auth on 2026-04-23 at 11:00 PT. Invite: Luis, Maya, infra lead (TBD).

Open questions (short)
- Do we pivot to a single canonical quickstart per language, or maintain both minimal + expanded versions? (Preference: start minimal, add "advanced" later).
- Who will own the daily smoke badge infra? Ops or DevExp? (Propose: DevExp owns infra for initial PoC.)

Quick links (copied for convenience)
- JS quickstart PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1423
- Docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/89
- JIRA: https://jira.redwood-inference.com/browse/DX-321

Status snapshot (one-line): Making steady progress on JS quickstart and docs PRs; Dedicated auth is the highest priority blocker this week; aim to unblock by 4/23 pairing session.

-- end of capture board --

(Notes: this doc is a lightweight working board — expect edits and inline comments. If you add action items, put your initials and a short ETA.)
